j.name: Abraham's journey
j.note: One family leaves the most advanced city of its age for a land it has never seen.
j.caution: The route is traditional; the sites of the camps are not all certain.

stops.note: Terah takes the family out of Ur toward Canaan.
They settle, Terah dies, and the call comes to Abram here.
First stop in Canaan, and the first promise of the land.
He pitches his tent and builds an altar between Bethel and Ai.
Famine drives him south — and into the lie about Sarai.
Back to the altar he had made at the first.
He settles by the oaks of Mamre, and buys a grave here for Sarah.
He returns here after Moriah, and lives out his years in the Negev.

j.name: The Exodus and the wilderness
j.note: Out of Egypt to Sinai, then forty years in the wilderness before the Jordan.
j.caution: Reconstructed. Almost every stop between Egypt and Kadesh is disputed, including which mountain is Sinai.

stops.note: They set out from the store-city they built.
The first camp out of Egypt.
On the edge of the wilderness, pillar of cloud ahead.
Bitter water made sweet — the first test after the sea.
Twelve springs and seventy palms.
Water from the rock, and the battle with Amalek.
The Law is given, and the covenant made.
The spies return; the people refuse; forty years begin here.
Aaron dies on the mountain, and Eleazar succeeds him.
On the plains of Moab, Moses sees the land and dies.

j.name: The exile and the return
j.note: The city falls, the people are carried east, and two generations later some come home.

stops.note: Babylon burns the Temple and breaks down the walls.
Zedekiah is sentenced here — the last thing he sees is his sons.
By the rivers of Babylon they sat down and wept.
Cyrus lets them go home; the Second Temple is finished by 516 BC.

j.name: The ministry of Jesus
j.note: Bethlehem to Jerusalem, by way of a carpenter's town nobody expected anything from.

stops.note: Born in the town of David, in a stable.
The family flees Herod and waits out his reign.
He grows up here, and is nearly thrown off its cliff for preaching.
Baptised by John, and the voice from heaven.
Water into wine — the first of the signs.
His base in Galilee: the synagogue, the paralytic, the centurion.
"Who do you say that I am?" — and Peter answers.
Blind Bartimaeus, and Zacchaeus up the tree.
Lazarus, come out.
The triumphal entry, the upper room, the cross, and the empty tomb.

j.name: Paul's first journey
j.note: Sent out from Antioch with Barnabas — and back the same way, strengthening what they planted.

stops.note: The church fasts, prays, and sends them off.
Down to the port and aboard.
They preach in the synagogues of Cyprus.
The proconsul believes; Elymas is struck blind.
John Mark leaves them here and goes home.
Pisidian Antioch — the great synagogue sermon, then expulsion.
A long stay, many believe, and a plot to stone them.
Taken for gods, then stoned and left for dead.
Many disciples made — and then they turn around and go back.
Down to the coast to sail home.
They report that God has opened a door to the Gentiles.

j.name: Paul's second journey
j.note: The journey that carried the gospel into Europe — because a door kept closing until one opened.

stops.note: He and Barnabas part over John Mark; Silas goes instead.
Back through the churches of the first journey.
Timothy joins them here.
The vision of the man of Macedonia: "Come over and help us."
Lydia, the slave girl, the earthquake, and the jailer's household.
Three sabbaths of reasoning from the Scriptures, then a riot.
They search the Scriptures daily to check what they are told.
The Areopagus, and the altar to an unknown god.
Eighteen months with Aquila and Priscilla; 1 Thessalonians is written here.
A brief stop, and a promise to return.
Ashore, up to greet the church, and home.
Back where he was sent from.

j.name: Paul's third journey
j.note: Three years in Ephesus, and then a long road to Jerusalem he was warned not to take.

stops.note: Out again, strengthening the disciples as he goes.
Two years in the hall of Tyrannus; all Asia hears the word.
Into Macedonia after the silversmiths' riot.
Three months in Greece; Romans is written here.
Eutychus falls from the window, and is raised.
He calls the Ephesian elders and says they will not see him again.
Disciples warn him through the Spirit not to go up.
Agabus binds his own hands with Paul's belt. Paul goes anyway.
Welcomed gladly — and arrested in the temple within days.

j.name: The voyage to Rome
j.note: A prisoner's appeal to Caesar, a hurricane, a shipwreck, and the gospel arriving in the capital in chains.

stops.note: Handed to a centurion of the Augustan Cohort.
Julius lets him visit friends and be cared for.
They transfer to an Alexandrian grain ship bound for Italy.
The wind refuses them; they run under the lee of Crete.
Paul warns them to winter here. They sail anyway.
Fourteen days in the storm, the ship broken up, and not one life lost.
Three days, after wintering on the island.
A south wind comes and carries them up the strait.
Ashore in Italy, and seven days with the brothers there.
The brothers come out to meet him; he thanks God and takes courage.
